OS: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS
systemd: systemd 255
captured: 2026-09-06T09:52:00Z
command: journalctl -t sudo -o json -n 5

Taken from a real server over LiteDeck's MCP run_command, then anonymised —
user, hostname, machine-id, boot-id and cursor were replaced. The shapes are
untouched, and they are the point of this fixture:

- Only one of the captured entries carried _COMM, _EXE, _SYSTEMD_UNIT and the
  _AUDIT_* fields. journald fills those by reading /proc/<pid>, and sudo has
  usually exited before it looks. A parser that expects them drops most rows.
- PWD, USER, COMMAND and TTY are not fields. They live inside MESSAGE as one
  " ; "-separated sentence, whose wording varies with the sudoers config.
- A refusal ("a password is required") uses the same sentence shape as a run,
  with the reason where TTY would be.

Two rows were added by hand on top of the capture, for cases the five real ones
did not cover: a COMMAND containing " ; " and a secret-looking flag, and a row
from an earlier boot so the boot boundary has something to find.
